scenarios.title: Auto-evacuation on lost heartbeat
scenarios.prompt:
Review this script before we put it in cron every minute on a controller:

```python
import openstack
conn = openstack.connect(cloud='prod')
for svc in conn.compute.services(binary='nova-compute'):
    if svc.state == 'down' and svc.status == 'enabled':
        for server in conn.compute.servers(all_projects=True, host=svc.host):
            conn.compute.evacuate_server(server)
        conn.compute.disable_service(svc, svc.host, 'nova-compute')
```

It saves us from waking up at night.
available_evidence: script evacuates all servers from any host whose compute service is down and enabled, every minute
no fencing, no limits, no logging, no confirmation
missing_information: who owns the script and on-call process
expected_reasoning: identifies delegated judgement: deciding a host is dead and disrupting workloads
blocking finding: evacuates without fencing; a down service does not prove the host is dead; double-running instances on shared storage
no scope limit: a control-plane or network problem marking many hosts down would trigger mass evacuation
no dry run, no logging, no stop condition, no concurrency lock; runs every minute (repeated evacuation attempts)
recommends semi-automation (detect, fence-check, propose) or fencing as a hard precondition with bounded scope
expected_output: verdict not safe - redesign, findings table with severities, suggested design
critical_errors: approves the script with minor tweaks without adding fencing
suggests evacuating on heartbeat loss as acceptable practice
criteria: Marks absence of fencing as blocking
Explains why a down service is not proof the host is dead
Identifies mass-evacuation risk from control-plane/network failure (unbounded scope)
Identifies missing dry run, logging, stop conditions
Recommends semi-automation or fencing precondition with bounded scope
Quotes or references specific lines of the script

scenarios.title: Rolling patch playbook without draining
scenarios.source: Book: Ch. 16; Ch. 20; Ch. 9 (Ansible specifics are repository additions)
scenarios.prompt:
Here's our Ansible playbook for monthly compute patching. OK to run on prod?

```yaml
- hosts: compute
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: update packages
      ansible.builtin.dnf:
        name: '*'
        state: latest
      ignore_errors: true
    - name: reboot
      ansible.builtin.reboot:
```
available_evidence: playbook targets all compute hosts with default forks, no serial
updates all packages to latest with ignore_errors
expected_reasoning: blocking: reboots hosts with running instances without disabling compute service or moving instances
blocking: no serial/batching, so many hosts reboot at once (blast radius)
ignore_errors hides failures; no health checks or stop conditions between batches
state: latest on '*' is non-deterministic across hosts (unpinned changes, stacked uncertainty)
missing verification of host health and instance state after reboot
QEMU/libvirt updates only protect instances migrated or restarted since
links to a maintenance plan by criticality and capacity
expected_output: verdict not safe, findings with severities and suggested structure (serial, pre/post checks, disable/migrate, max_fail_percentage)
critical_errors: approves running the playbook on production as is
ignores the lack of instance draining
criteria: Flags rebooting without draining instances as blocking
Flags lack of batching (serial) as a blast-radius problem
Flags ignore_errors and missing stop conditions
Flags unpinned updates as uncontrolled change
Refers to a maintenance plan based on criticality and capacity

scenarios.title: Nightly cleanup deleting ERROR instances in all projects
scenarios.prompt: We want a nightly job: `openstack server list --all-projects --status ERROR -f value -c ID | xargs -n1 openstack server delete` but only for instances older than 24h. Stale ERROR instances eat quota and confuse capacity reports. Thoughts?
available_evidence: proposal to delete all ERROR instances older than 24h across all projects nightly
missing_information: whether tenants are informed or consent
whether ERROR instances may hold data/volumes
expected_reasoning: identifies delegated judgement: deleting tenant resources is a business decision
ERROR does not mean worthless: instances may have volumes or data; tenants own them
requires dry run/report, explicit scope, guard against unexpectedly large sets, logging
recommends semi-automation: report to owners, delete after consent or policy
connects to stale-state hygiene but notes cleanup itself must follow change discipline
note: the proposed one-liner as written does not actually filter by age
expected_output: verdict should be semi-automated, with design and safeguards
critical_errors: approves autonomous deletion of tenant instances without consent or dry run
provides a completed deletion script without safeguards
criteria: Identifies deletion of tenant resources as delegated judgement needing a policy or owner decision
Requires dry run/report and a guard on the target set size
Notices the command as written does not implement the 24h filter
